title: Choose Armarium's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Tape-Trade Zine. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tape-Trade Zine
options.thesis: The collection kept like a photocopied zine's tape list: typed, stamped, cut and pasted, in toner black and copy-paper white.
options.viewport: Each library a xeroxed page: cut-paper masthead, typed tape-list rows, covers as halftone thumbs that turn full colour on focus, states rubber-stamped.
options.risk: Reads as costume if the grit leaks into controls; text must stay typewriter-crisp and the grain stay in the ground.

raised.raise: Covers are the only full colour on the page; everything else is toner.
State rides one variable everywhere: the stamp (none, READING, READ, MISSING, BROKEN).
Destructive acts (revoke a token, mark unread) take a marked two-step commit.
Rows unfold in place into the full item record instead of navigating away.
The text field stays achromatic; red lives only in stamps and the focus edge.

options.label: Accession Register
options.lineage: library card catalogues and accession ledgers
options.thesis: The collection as a working library's register: drawer tabs, ruled ledger columns, date-due stamps.
options.viewport: Drawer-front tabs for the libraries across the top, a ruled ledger of items with accession numbers, shelfmarks and stamped status, small covers at the left edge.
options.risk: The most familiar direction on the table: card-catalogue nostalgia is where library tools usually land.

options.label: Timetable Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size for everything; rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule.
options.viewport: One continuous rack of library blocks; items as departure lines with format codes and filled or hollow status marks.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for dense management (formats as codes, state as marks); loses on audience identification.
options.risk: The rake and single size fight long book titles and 13,000-item scrolls.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of artwork; the focused tile grows and tells you what it is.
options.viewport: Horizontal rails per library, metadata only inside the focused tile.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the Plex/Kavita look being replaced, and it hides the state management needs.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the media servers it replaces.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth: brightness, spacing and drift, never boxes.
options.viewport: One still ivory line of work over drifting layers.
options.case: Loses both axes: drift and no-enclosure fight a dense management table.
options.kept: State carried by one consistent variable.

options.label: Darkroom Bay
options.thesis: Work moves through stations; past marked points it is irreversible.
options.case: Loses both axes: the collection has no station pipeline.
options.kept: Marked commit points before irreversible acts.
options.risk: A metaphor with no job here.

options.label: Miura Sheet
options.thesis: One pull deploys a packet into a full field.
options.case: Loses both axes: folding geometry adds nothing to finding a book.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: Colour lives only at the edge; the field stays white.
options.case: Loses both axes: pastel science-journal register, far from the owner's world.
options.kept: Colour confined to edges and covers.
options.risk: Too faint for state at a glance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What self-hosted media servers ship (Kavita, Komga, Jellyfin), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Library sidebar, a dark poster grid, a detail drawer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the apps it replaces, by design.
